thesis: Coding assistant pilots stall around day 90 because teams count seat activation instead of changed work, so the fix is one agreed measure with a named owner from week one.

anecdotes.summary: Central story: fintech two-team pilot, opens and closes talk.
Author's 2024 pilot: no measurement owner until budget cut.

claims.statement: Abstract: Halvorsen Research's 2026 report on 32 companies.
Slide 2: Halvorsen Research interviewed 32 companies for a 2026 report on platform teams. The median pilot ran 94 days before a renewal decision.
Slide 3: Northfield surveyed 1,240 developers in March 2026. 61% said their company's assistant pilot had "no agreed success measure" at launch.
Slide 4: Among pilots with no success measure, weekly active use fell from 78% in month one to 41% by month three. Among pilots that had one, it fell from 80% to 66%.
Slide 6: 9 of Halvorsen's 32 companies tracked any change in cycle time or review load during the pilot. All 9 renewed.
Slide 7: The other 23 companies tracked only seat activation. 11 of them renewed.
Slide 11: The 9 Halvorsen companies that all renewed tracked any change in cycle time or review load.
Abstract and slide 8: A 2025 Ostrava University study of 400 pull requests found no measurable change in review time with assistant use.
Slide 12: If the line didn't move, as with the 400 pull requests in the Ostrava study, recommend stopping.
Slide 13: The median pilot gets 94 days.

gaps: The fintech team's actual review turnaround figures (before and after), needed for the closing slide's visual and notes; marked TK on slide 13.
